propositions: The enrich drain advisory lock is held across multi-minute LLM calls (437s and 131s observed), causing every spawned drain child to skip with lock-held status and creating a standing backlog of ~1,046 entries while the max drain throughput is 5 tickets per multi-minute exclusive hold

Restructuring drain() into three phases (collect under lock, enrich with lock released, finalize without drain lock) with concurrency guard (cap 3 distinct live-lease drainers) and lease-derived batch clamp (max(1, lease_ttl_s // 40) ≈ 20–25 items) reduces lock hold from 437s to ~9.8s per item and enables concurrent drainers

Stale ticket rewrites between claim and finalize must skip the digest emit and re-enqueue immediately (soak 0) without duplicate LLM calls, verified by snapshot revalidation of content_hash at finalize time
DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH must be raised from 5 to 20 with a lease-derived upper bound so no batch outlives its lease mid-run, preventing lease-expiry crashes and unbounded LLM call blast radius

Concurrent drainers bounded by concurrency guard return skipped status when >= 3 distinct live-lease drainer_ids exist, preventing runaway parallelism while allowing up to 3 × 20-item batches to process lock-free

The drain restructure is behavior-preserving: existing failure disposition, self-heal, queue event schema (ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE), has_pending_enrichment semantics, MCP surface, and operation-linked trigger remain unchanged
